sheet-28.description: Sheet 28 of the Harrison, East Newark and Kearny series covers the riverfront of East Newark and the adjoining part of Harrison, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned on the page so that north points to the right and the Passaic River runs along the top. Passaic Avenue follows the river bank across the sheet; below it lie the blocks between New Street, Reynolds Avenue, Searing Avenue and Mulock Place, closed at the bottom by Grant Avenue, with a further row of lots between Grant Avenue and John Street. The boundary between the Borough of East Newark and the Town of Harrison is marked as a dash-dot line running along Reynolds Avenue and diagonally across the blocks toward Searing Avenue. Along the river are the works of the New Jersey Adamant Manufacturing Company (plaster board, kilns, sand house), the lumber yard of E. W. McClave and Son, and the building material yard of Van Keuren and Son. Between Passaic Avenue and Grant Avenue are the John Newey pearl button factory, Pomeroy Brothers' inks and wax works, a second-hand lumber storage yard of Van Keuren and Son, a coal yard of D. Dunn Jr., blacksmith and carpenter shops, and rows of dwellings, flats, tenements and saloons along Reynolds Avenue, Searing Avenue and Mulock Place. At the left edge the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad (Morris and Essex Division) curves across Passaic Avenue and Hamilton Street on its approach to the river crossing. Much of the block next to the railroad is drawn empty.
notes: New Street, between the railroad and Reynolds Avenue, no longer exists; the area west of Reynolds Avenue is now crossed by Interstate 280 (Essex Freeway).
Passaic Avenue west of Reynolds Avenue has been realigned; the modern road leaves the drawn line toward the railroad.
The sheet carries pasted corrections (Van Keuren and Son Inc., a temporary location of a hydrant), so it reflects a later revision than 1907 in places.
Placed from six street junctions on the east half of the sheet; the west half (railroad and New Street) has no control.

Map, 50 ft. East Newark/Harrison: Passaic Av along the Passaic River (top), New St, Reynolds Av, Searing Av, Mulock Pl, Grant Av, John St, Hamilton St; DL&W (M&E Div) railroad at left; E. Newark/Harrison line. Sheet turned (north to the right). One part.

sheet-29-1.description: The lower part of sheet 29 shows the southern end of East Newark between Central Avenue (at the top, along the heavy line that divides the sheet) and Mulock Place, from the Passaic River on the left to Grant Avenue on the right, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. A bridge to Newark leaves the river bank at Central Avenue. Between the river and Passaic Avenue are the Pure Oil Company storage tanks and warehouse and the building material yard of Van Keuren and Son, with a lime and cement shed. East of Passaic Avenue the block between Central Avenue and President Street is laid out in narrow house lots, mostly still empty, with a row of dwellings, flats and a saloon along Grant Avenue. South of President Street the Louis Hartung Passaic River Boiler Works, a Public Service Corporation substation, dwellings and a circular storage reservoir stand at the west end, while the eastern half of the block is filled by the works of the Stewart Hartshorn Company, makers of self-acting shade rollers: wire drawing, spring winding, rolling mill, tempering, pickling and plating rooms, and wood roller storage and assembly buildings, with an iron bridge over Mulock Place to its buildings on the next sheet. The East Newark and Harrison boundary is marked at the lower right corner, where the sheet edge is torn.
notes: The lower right corner of the scan is torn away, below Mulock Place at Grant Avenue.

Central Avenue is drawn with its north edge on the dividing line of the sheet; its junctions carry about 2 m residuals and the modern approach to the Clay Street bridge may differ from the drawn line.

Map, 50 ft, two parts separated by a double line at Bergen Av. Part 1 (lower): East Newark, Passaic Av, Central Av, President St, Mulock Pl, Grant Av, Stewart Hartshorn Co. works, Passaic River at left. Part 2 (upper): New Jersey Home for Disabled Soldiers, Kearny, between Bergen Av, Belgrove Drive and Afton St.

sheet-29-2.description: The upper part of sheet 29 shows the grounds of the New Jersey Home for Disabled Soldiers in Kearny, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. The block is bounded by Bergen Avenue along the bottom (cut by the heavy line dividing the sheet), Belgrove Drive on the right and Afton Street at the top, whose name is cut off by the sheet edge. Most of the grounds are open lawn. Along the Belgrove Drive side stand four long dormitory buildings, a laundry, a dining room with assembly room above and a kitchen, all joined by a covered walk to a cross-shaped hospital of four wards (A to D), with an administration building, a morgue, a boiler house and small outbuildings. Gate houses stand at the west edge of the grounds. Each building is lettered A to Q. The streets beyond the grounds are not drawn; Passaic Avenue, the western boundary, lies just off the left edge of the sheet.
notes: Placed from a single junction (Belgrove Drive and Bergen Avenue, measured from Belgrove's edges and Bergen's drawn north edge) with the rotation of its drawn lines and the atlas scale; low confidence.
Afton Street and Passaic Avenue junctions fall just off the sheet.

Map, 50 ft, two parts separated by a double line at Bergen Av. Part 2 (upper): New Jersey Home for Disabled Soldiers, Kearny, between Bergen Av, Belgrove Drive and Afton St.

sheet-30.description: Sheet 30 covers a residential district straddling the boundary between the Town of Harrison and the Borough of East Newark, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north to the right. Grant Avenue runs along the top, followed by John Street, North 2nd Street and North 3rd Street, crossed by William Street on the left and Central Avenue on the right; the town line runs down the middle of the sheet as a dash-dot line. The blocks are closely built with two- and three-storey dwellings, flats, tenements and saloons on narrow lots, numbered along each street. Near Grant Avenue are a warehouse of the Stewart Hartshorn Company with a 100,000 gallon reservoir, a coal and wagon yard and a lumber yard; the company's shade roller works themselves appear only in outline at the top, referred to sheet 29. In the lower left, where William Street bends and Cross Street runs diagonally to North 3rd Street, the small triangular blocks hold junk shops, a tin shop, a carpenter's shop, a hall, a pool room and lumber sheds. Below North 3rd Street the neighbouring sheets 18, 19 and 33 are indicated only by their outlines.
notes: Map, 50 ft. Harrison and East Newark: Grant Av, John St, N. 2nd St, N. 3rd St, William St, Cross St, Central Av. One part.

sheet-31.description: Sheet 31 shows the mills of the Clark Thread Company in East Newark and the adjoining edge of Kearny, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. It is bounded by Johnston Avenue at the top, Grant Avenue on the right and Central Avenue at the bottom, with Passaic Avenue running down the left side and the Passaic River beyond it. The Erie Railroad (Newark and Paterson Branch) crosses the top of the sheet below Johnston Avenue, with the Erie coal yard of R. J. Whyte, a row of dwellings, flats and saloons, and the Kearny and East Newark boundary along a brick wall. The main block holds the Clark Thread Company's cotton mills, thread mills, cotton storage houses, picker houses, engine and boiler houses and a tall chimney. South of Orchard Street, marked closed, are the mills of the Clark Mile End Spool Cotton Company, with spooling, carding, spinning and twisting rooms, machine shops and offices. Between Passaic Avenue and the river are another Clark Thread Company works with a bleach house and making up room, a coal pile under an automatic railway elevator, and a derrick on the bank. Lincoln Avenue and Sherman Avenue are drawn north of Johnston Avenue, where the neighbouring sheets 41 and 42 begin.
notes: Sherman Avenue north of Johnston Avenue is today Sheridan Avenue (OpenStreetMap).
Orchard Street is marked closed on the sheet and no longer exists.
Passaic Avenue between Johnston Avenue and Central Avenue has been realigned; its junctions fit 3 m off.
Four of the six control points were hand-picked: the streets around the mill blocks have few solid edges for the detector.

Map, 50 ft. East Newark and Kearny: Clark Thread Co. and Clark Mile End Spool Cotton Co. mills between Passaic Av, Grant Av, Johnston Av and Central Av; Orchard St (closed); Erie RR Newark & Paterson branch; Passaic River at left. One part.

sheet-32.description: Sheet 32 covers the northeastern part of East Newark and the adjoining edges of Kearny and Harrison, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. Johnston Avenue runs along the top and Central Avenue along the bottom, crossed by Grant Avenue on the left, John Street, North 2nd Street and North 3rd Street, with Kearny Avenue and North 4th Street at the right edge; Highland Avenue and Maple Street are drawn north of Johnston Avenue. The Erie Railroad (Newark and Paterson Branch) crosses the sheet below Johnston Avenue and is carried over Kearny Avenue on a steel bridge; the Kearny and East Newark boundary runs just south of the tracks. Between the railroad and Sherman Avenue are the Chemical Charcoal Company's sheds, the John Hewitt Foundry Company's iron foundry, a coal yard of S. Smith Coal Company and the East Newark fire station and borough hall. South of Sherman Avenue the blocks are filled with two- and three-storey dwellings and flats; institutions include the North Reformed Church's Kearny Chapel and St. Anthony's Church, and there are the T. Gleeson wire weaving works and the F. W. Worstmann Company machine shop. The block east of North 3rd Street, crossed by Davis Street and the East Newark and Harrison boundary, is left blank and belongs to sheet 33.
notes: North 4th Street is today Frank E. Rodgers Boulevard North; the modern road does not follow the drawn line closely and was not used for control.
John Street ends at Sherman Avenue on the sheet; the modern John Street continues north to Grant Avenue.
Map, 50 ft. East Newark/Kearny/Harrison: Johnston Av, Sherman Av, Central Av, Grant Av, John St, N. 2nd St, N. 3rd St, Kearny Av, N. 4th St, Davis St; Erie RR. One part.
